chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed and Ibn Abi Umeyr, altogether from Jameel ibn Darraj, from a man, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them).

Regarding a man who stole, or drank wine, or committed adultery, so he was not known to be with that and he was not seized, until he repented and corrected himself. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When his correctness is recognized from him, it is a beautiful matter, the Hadd (penalty) would not be established upon him.'

Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr said, 'I said, 'So if it was a matter close by, would the Hadd not be established?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was five months or less from it, and he had manifested a beautiful matter, the Huddud (penalties) would not be established upon him.'
And that has been reported from some of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them).

key_terms.أَمْرٌ جَمِيلٌ: A beautiful matter (manifestation of good character/reformation)

ai.seo_question: Under what conditions is the Hadd penalty waived for someone who committed a crime but repented before being caught?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'sitr' (concealment) and the preference for divine pardon over public punishment when reformation is evident. Scholars note that the 'five months' timeframe serves as a practical benchmark for assessing the stability of the individual's repentance, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on mercy and the potential for spiritual recovery over rigid legalism.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed and Ibn Abu Umeyr, altogether from Jameel Bin Darraj, from a man, (It has been narrated) from one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws), regarding a man who steals, or drinks the wine, or commits adultery, so he was not know to be with that and he was not seized, until he repented and corrected (himself). So heasws said: ‘When his correctness is recognised from him, it is a beautiful matter, the Penalty (Hadd) would not be established upon him’.

Muhammad Bin Abu Umeyr said, ‘I said, ‘So if it was a matter close by (just been committed), (the Penalty (Hadd)) would not be established?’ Heasws said: ‘If it was five or six months from it, and he had manifested a beautiful matter (reformed himself), the Penalties would not be established upon him’.
And that has been reported from some of our companions,
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>).
